{{nihongo|'''Utsumochi Shrine'''|宇都母知神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Sagami Province]].

'''Utsumochi Shrine''' (うつもちじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Uchimoto, {{ill|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|Q386661|qid=Q386661}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|Q127513|qid=Q127513}}. It is regarded as one of the shrines (minor shrine) listed among the thirteen {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Sagami Province|Q11582137|qid=Q11582137|lt=Engishiki shrines}} of {{ill|Sagami Province|Q1053732|qid=Q1053732}} recorded in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'' of {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Engi}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}).<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1273537/73?tocOpened=1 |title=''Engishiki Vol. 2 (Volumes 8, 9, 10)'', Nihon Koten Zenshū Kankōkai, Showa 4. Frame 73. ({{ill|National Diet Library Digital Collections|Q117959850|qid=Q117959850}}) |publisher= |accessdate=2018-09-03 }}</ref>

=== Enshrined deities ===
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu Omikami}}
* {{ill|Wakumusubi|qid=Q10921330|lt=Wakumusubi-no-Kami}}
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wakahinakabe-no-Mikoto}}

=== Origin and History ===
The exact date of the shrine’s founding is unknown, but there is a record that solemn {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=rituals}} were conducted in the 3rd year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Q357235|qid=Q357235}} (according to the {{ill|Japanese imperial year|Q1209728|qid=Q1209728|lt=Imperial Year}} 1119<ref>Stone monument within the shrine grounds</ref>{{Refnest|group="Note"|The Utsumochi Shrine page (Kanagawa Prefecture Shrine Office website, viewed September 20, 2017) states {{ill|495|Q30806|qid=Q30806}}.<ref name="kanajin-utsumochi" />}}) (''Nihon Sōkoku {{ill|Fudoki|Q1194534|qid=Q1194534}}''). Although there are no records of relocation, the same fudoki states that the shrine was located in “Utsumochi-go, Takakura District, Sagami Province.”<ref name="kanajin-utsumochi">{{Cite web|Japanese book|author= |url=http://www.kanagawa-jinja.or.jp/search_dtl.php4?jid=573&cd=1206054&scd=&npg=0 |title=Utsumochi Shrine |date=|publisher=Kanagawa Prefecture Shrine Office |accessdate=2017-09-20 }}</ref> In the ''Engishiki Jinmyōchō'', it is recorded as “Utsumochi Shrine, one of the six shrines in {{ill|Kōza District, Kanagawa|Q1202776|qid=Q1202776}} among the thirteen shrines of Sagami Province (shikinaisha).”

In {{ill|Tengyō|Q1327340|qid=Q1327340}} 2 ({{ill|939|Q23422|qid=Q23422}}), the spirit of Wakahinakabe-no-Mikoto was transferred from {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}{{ill|Hase|Q11396531|qid=Q11396531|lt=Hase}} and enshrined together in the {{ill|Aidono|Q135009883|qid=Q135009883}}. In {{ill|Shōō (Kamakura period)|Q1327371|qid=Q1327371}} 3 ({{ill|1290|Q5552|qid=Q5552}}), {{ill|Hōjō Sadatoki|Q3136681|qid=Q3136681}}, regent ({{ill|Shikken|Q1045904|qid=Q1045904}}) of the eighth shogun {{ill|Prince Hisaaki|Q715826|qid=Q715826}} of the {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|Q736839|qid=Q736839}}, rebuilt the shrine buildings. Later, in {{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}} 4 ({{ill|1627|Q6833|qid=Q6833}}), the local lord {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takagi Mondo Minamoto no Masatsugu}} donated 900 tsubo (about 3,000 {{ill|Square metre|Q25343|qid=Q25343|lt=m<sup>2</sup>}}) of shrine land and rebuilt the main hall. During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, the shrine was also known as “Daijingū” and “Shinmeigū.”

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it was ranked as a village shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}. In {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 12 ({{ill|1923|Q2169|qid=Q2169}}), the shrine buildings (built in {{ill|Ansei|Q1327259|qid=Q1327259}} 5 <small>({{ill|1858|Q7684|qid=Q7684}})</small>) were completely destroyed, including the main hall, due to the {{ill|aftermath of 1923 Great Kantō earthquake|Q3742341|qid=Q3742341}}. However, they were fully restored three years later in Taishō 15 ({{ill|1926|ab|1926|af|1926|als|1926|am|1926 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1926|ar|1926|ary|1926|arz|1926|ast|1926|av|1926 сон|avk|1926|az|1926|azb|۱۹۲۶ (میلادی)|ba|1926 йыл|ban|1926|bar|1926|bat_smg|1926|bcl|1926|be|1926|be_x_old|1926|bg|1926|bh|1926|bn|১৯২৬|bpy|মারি ১৯২৬|br|1926|bs|1926.|ca|1926|cdo|1926 nièng|ce|1926 шо|ceb|1926|ckb|١٩٢٦|co|1926|crh|1926|cs|1926|csb|1926|cv|1926|cy|1926|da|1926|de|1926|diq|1926|dsb|1926|el|1926|eml|1926|eo|1926|es|1926|et|1926|eu|1926|ext|1926|fa|۱۹۲۶|fi|1926|fiu_vro|1926|fo|1926|fr|1926|frp|1926|frr|1926|fur|1926|fy|1926|ga|1926|gag|1926|gan|1926年|gcr|1926|gd|1926|gl|1926|gn|1926|gv|1926|hak|1926-ngièn|he|1926|hi|१९२६|hif|1926|hr|1926.|hsb|1926|ht|1926 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1926|hy|1926|hyw|1926 թուական|ia|1926|id|1926|ilo|1926|inh|1926 шу|io|1926|is|1926|it|1926|ja|1926年|jbo|1926moi|jv|1926|ka|1926|kaa|1926|kbp|1926|kk|1926 жыл|kn|೧೯೨೬|ko|1926년|krc|1926 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1926|ku|1926|kv|1926-ӧд во|kw|1926|la|1926|lb|1926|lez|1926 йис|li|1926|lij|1926|lmo|1926|ln|1926|lt|1926 m.|lv|1926. gads|mai|१९२६|map_bms|1926|mdf|1926|mg|1926|mhr|1926|mi|1926|min|1926|mk|1926|ml|1926|mn|1926 он|mr|इ.स. १९२६|mrj|1926 и|ms|1926|my|၁၉၂၆|myv|1926 ие|mzn|۱۹۲۶|nah|1926|nap|1926|nds|1926|nds_nl|1926|new|ई सं १९२६|nl|1926|nn|1926|no|1926|nov|1926|nrm|1926|nso|1926|oc|1926|olo|1926|or|୧୯୨୬|os|1926-æм аз|pa|1926|pam|1926|pap|1926|pl|1926|pnb|1926|pt|1926|qu|1926|ro|1926|roa_rup|1926|roa_tara|1926|ru|1926 год|rue|1926|sah|1926 сыл|sc|1926|scn|1926|sco|1926|sd|1926ع|se|1926|sh|1926.|shn|1926|simple|1926|sk|1926|sl|1926|smn|1926|sq|1926|sr|1926|stq|1926|su|1926|sv|1926|sw|1926|szl|1926|ta|1926|te|1926|tg|Соли 1926|th|พ.ศ. 2469|tk|1926|tl|1926|tly|1926|tpi|1926|tr|1926|tt|1926 ел|ty|1926|udm|1926 ар|ug|1926 - The temple bell at the {{ill|Shōrō|de|Shōrō|es|Shōrō|eu|Shōrō|fr|Shōrō|id|Shōrō|it|Shōrō|ja|鐘楼|wuu|钟楼（东亚）|zh|鐘樓 (東亞)|qid=Q1363585}} located just across the road west of the {{ill|keidai|ja|境内|qid=Q11429002}} was offered in the spring of {{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ka|შოვას პერიოდი|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567}} 20 ({{ill|1945|Q5240|qid=Q5240}}) for material collection during the {{ill|Pacific War|Q184425|qid=Q184425}}, and was not installed for some time, but was rebuilt in {{ill|1975|Q2479|qid=Q2479}}. === Reservoir ===
At 2009 Ōdaira, Uchimoto, there is a shrine-owned {{ill|irrigation reservoir|Q112083751|qid=Q112083751}} (about 150 m<sup>2</sup>).<ref name="kanajin-utsumochi" />

=== Origin of the Place Name ===
One theory regarding the origin of the local place name (Uchimoto) is that it derived from “Uzumochi” (宇豆毛遅) of Utsumochi Shrine, which became corrupted into “Uchimodori.” In {{ill|archaic language|Q11411592|qid=Q11411592}}, both “utsu” and “mochi” are said to mean “small {{ill|Basin (geomorphology)|Q813672|qid=Q813672}},” and it is believed that the area was first called “Utsumochi” due to its topography, which later changed into “Uchimodori.” Another theory holds that when the swordsmith {{ill|Masamune|Q708935|qid=Q708935|lt=Gorō Masamune}} from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ebina}} was traveling to {{ill|Kamakura|Q10939227|qid=Q10939227}}, he rested in this area and, dissatisfied with the sword he was about to present, “returned home to reforge it,” which became the origin of the place name.<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://www.city.fujisawa.kanagawa.jp/gosho-c/data15331.shtml |title=History of Goshomi: Origin of Place Names |accessdate=August 29, 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140821214356/http://www.city.fujisawa.kanagawa.jp/gosho-c/data15331.shtml |archivedate=August 21, 2014 }} - {{ill|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|Q386661|qid=Q386661}}</ref><ref>[Story of Uchimoto] (Fujisawa City Machizukuri Association)</ref>

=== Access ===
* From the west exit of {{ill|Shōnandai Station|Q1036357|qid=Q1036357}} on the {{ill|Odakyū Enoshima Line|Q1063924|qid=Q1063924}}, {{ill|Sōtetsu Izumino Line|Q846367|qid=Q846367}}, or {{ill|Yokohama Municipal Subway Blue Line|Q841360|qid=Q841360}}:
** {{ill|Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu|Q10854960|qid=Q10854960|lt=Kanachu}} Bus ({{ill|Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu Ayase Branch|Q11588892|qid=Q11588892}}): For Ayase Depot via Keio University and Miyahara; get off at “Utsumochi Shrine Entrance,” 3-minute walk.
** Kanachu Bus ({{ill|Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu Ayase Branch|Q11588892|qid=Q11588892}}): Twin Liner Express for Keio University; get off at “Keio Junior and Senior High School,” 10-minute walk.
* From the north exit of {{ill|Tsujidō Station|Q1049779|qid=Q1049779}} on the {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|Q499071|qid=Q499071|lt=JR}} line:
** Kanachu Bus ({{ill|Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu Ayase Branch|Q11588892|qid=Q11588892}}): For Keio University; get off at “Keio University,” 15-minute walk.

=== Notes ===
There are often no staff at the {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}}, and telephone inquiries may not be possible. If you wish to receive a {{ill|Shuin|Q7504772|qid=Q7504772}}, it is more reliable to visit during festivals or New Year when events are being held.

There are also {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=toilets}} installed within the shrine grounds.
